say.en: Amul began when dairy farmers in Gujarat joined hands so that middlemen could not cheat them. A cooperative is owned by the people it serves. In this lesson: State the features of a cooperative society.
Describe the types of cooperative societies.
Evaluate the merits and limitations of cooperatives.

body.en: A cooperative society is a voluntary association of persons who join together to promote their common economic interests on the basis of equality. *Features*: voluntary membership (open to all, free to leave), a minimum of ten adult members, compulsory registration under the Cooperative Societies Act, 1912 or a state act, which gives it a separate legal entity, limited liability (to the capital contributed), democratic control (one member, one vote, whatever the shares held) and a service motive rather than profit maximisation; any surplus is distributed in proportion to members' business with the society, and a part is set aside for reserves and welfare.

body.en: *Merits*: equality in voting, limited liability, stable existence (not affected by members leaving), economy of operations through voluntary service and fewer middlemen, government support (loans, tax concessions) and ease of formation. Limitations: limited capital (members are usually of modest means), management problems (honorary managers may lack skill), lack of secrecy (affairs are discussed openly), excessive government control and audit, and differences of opinion among members.

say.en: Sort each feature of cooperatives.

problem.en: How is a cooperative different from a partnership? Give four points.

steps.en: Members: a cooperative needs at least 10; a partnership 2 to 50.
Registration: compulsory for a cooperative; optional for a partnership.
Liability: limited for cooperative members; unlimited for partners.
Control: one member one vote in a cooperative; partners usually by agreement and capital.

answer.en: They differ in members, registration, liability and voting.
